title: Contributory negligence - its effect on the final compensation
p1: A small mistake by an injured person can sometimes change the amount of compensation they receive. But many people are surprised to learn that even when someone else is responsible for an accident, the final payment may not always be the full amount.
p2: A common misconception is that proving another person's fault automatically guarantees complete compensation. In reality, contributory negligence means the injured person’s own actions are also considered if they helped cause or worsen the damage. Even a minor contribution to the incident can reduce the final compensation.
p3: For example, if a court finds that a person was 20% responsible for their injuries due to their own carelessness, the compensation may be reduced by that percentage. The key takeaway is simple: responsibility is often shared, and every action before an accident can matter. Knowing this can help people make safer decisions and understand how claims are evaluated.
conclusion: Do you think compensation should always be reduced when the injured person shares some responsibility, even if another party caused the accident?
